title: NIST FIPS 186-5
verification: Private-key generation and public-key verification are distinct processes; accepting origin evidence requires identity/key assurances. Hash processing depends on the signature algorithm. No RSA-specific encryption recipe or human-intent guarantee is appropriate.

title: Microsoft TPM recommendations
location: TPM design and implementation; Discrete, Integrated, or Firmware TPM?
verification: TPM implementations include discrete, integrated and firmware designs; security properties and platform integration vary.

title: Microsoft secure Windows boot process
verification: Boot-signature policy is enforced by firmware; measurements are recorded using the TPM and may support attestation. Recording is not itself the same operation as enforcing boot acceptance.

title: Microsoft BitLocker FAQ
location: Can I use BitLocker on an operating system drive without a TPM?
verification: The volume master key may be released by the TPM. A platform key protected within the TPM must not be confused with every drive-decryption key remaining forever outside OS memory.

title: YubiHSM 2 product overview
location: Overview; Key backup and transfer; FIPS Validation; FIPS Mode
verification: USB is a documented form factor; protected backup/transfer exists; certification and approved mode apply to named versions, not every HSM. Performance is a device/workload property, not a category constant.

title: NIST CMVP certificate 5302
location: Module name, standard, level, caveat and Security Policy
verification: The actual certificate names a module and approved configuration. This is an evidence example, not a product recommendation or a claim every HSM has that level.

title: NIST FIPS 140-3
location: Abstract: four qualitative security levels and covered areas
verification: Security requirements cover several areas and levels; physical/tamper and key-management properties require the selected module policy. Do not promise instant zeroization for every HSM.

title: ISC2 CC exam outline
verification: Use as a scope reference. Hardware/signature details here explain the existing beginner concepts, not mandatory algorithm mathematics or certified-module procurement knowledge.
